content: Specifically, demand from Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) demonstrated a consistent and overall increasing trend, beginning at a minimum value of 120.0 million tons in 2020 and reaching a maximum volume of 155.0 million tons by 2023. This expansion highlights the heavy reliance of major automotive manufacturers on scalable and reliable transport logistics to maintain global supply chains. Similarly, the aftermarket parts segment exhibited a parallel upward trajectory, growing from 45.0 million tons in 2020 to 58.0 million tons in 2023. The simultaneous growth in both the OEM and aftermarket parts segments illustrates a compounding demand for transport services, driven by both new vehicle production and the ongoing maintenance requirements of the existing global vehicle fleet. The client profiles within these expanding segments are increasingly defined by their rigorous demands for operational efficiency, technological integration, and high-value freight care. While explicit, granular client case studies are somewhat limited in recent literature, overarching industry trends indicate that e-commerce expansion and the critical need for efficient fleet management are primary drivers influencing client types and their respective service expectations [41] [45] . Clients operating in the modern automotive supply chain require logistics partners capable of ensuring timely delivery and the meticulous handling of high-value freight, a standard that has been heavily emphasized in specialized transport sectors such as air cargo logistics [35] . Furthermore, professional handling and secure transportation of automotive freight have been established as baseline expectations for clients entrusting valuable assets to transport providers [42] . To meet the sophisticated needs of these client profiles, transport providers are increasingly investing in fleet modernization and advanced technological solutions. Modern transport solutions, such as the 2026 Ford Transit Commercial Cargo Van, illustrate the industry's shift toward technologically equipped fleets, offering features like Android Auto and Apple CarPlay that enhance driver connectivity and operational efficiency [43] . Clients now segment transport providers based on their technological capabilities, favoring those who can offer real-time tracking, predictive maintenance, and automated logistics management.
